limitations: Koffi materials contain the exact locked published main npm archive, including its FFI sources, ABI assembly, cnoke/CMake build inputs and vendored Node-API/addon headers. The catalog and extracted notices identify only the bytes in that published archive.

The three Koffi platform registry receipts bind their exact optional-package declarations and lock integrities. No original platform producer job, compiler closure, separate libffi dependency or rebuild is inferred from those declarations.

Canvas materials contain the complete own src and skia-c directories at b2723ffae4e74e8c9df752902b137ec4061530e9, their original Git trees/blobs, actual root build/lock/config and named helper inputs, original GitHub identity/run/job responses and original npm registry/attestation responses for the main and three platform packages.

Canvas SLSA payload subjects are checked against the exact package-lock SHA-512 and registry integrity and their declared source/run are checked against the archived Git receipts. This is an association check, not independent signature, certificate, transparency-log or trust-root verification.

The Canvas workflow publishes packages after collecting matrix artifacts and downloading separately built Skia libraries. Its provenance does not identify or supply the original external Skia asset producer, library bytes or every transitive native constituent.

Original Skia root LICENSE and DEPS and the depot_tools root LICENSE are bound to the exact Canvas-declared Gitlinks and repositories. Only these related-source fragments are supplied: complete Skia/depot_tools and other selected native third-party sources and notices remain outside this slice. The ten downloaded Skia static libraries and Windows ICU data are named by the source/recipe, not supplied as historical build inputs here.

The held own native directories include their C++ header and checked-in Rust source inputs. Root Cargo/package/Yarn/target configuration, rust-toolchain.toml and named helper sources are held. The Dockerfile and C++ runtime helper are repository sources at this commit, not recovered records that the external asset producer executed them. No SDK/container/toolchain closure is supplied by those manifests; the external Yarn CLI selected by .yarnrc.yml and other tool distributions remain outside this slice.

These materials do not establish complete corresponding source, all native-component license responsibilities, a binary rebuild, identical historical output or historical toolchain replay. No license-compatibility conclusion is made.

The five supplied published Cargo archives are exactly the mimalloc-safe/libmimalloc-sys2 and libavif/libavif-sys/libaom-sys versions in the original Canvas Cargo.lock. Their SHA-256, original version-registry responses, complete published file catalogs, VCS metadata and extracted original notices are checked together. This is not the source closure of every Cargo.lock entry or every native constituent.

Archive member notices describe the actual published source containers, including target-specific and unselected vendor content. Canvas does not select mimalloc v3, libavif-sys disables libyuv and libsharpyuv in its held build input, and libaom-sys can accept external static-library paths. The held sources do not recover the original producer environment or prove that every bundled third-party directory was linked.

The libavif-sys and libaom-sys archives omit their own repository root LICENSE. Original root notices are additionally supplied at the exact VCS bases declared in those archives, with original Git commit/tree/blob receipts. libaom-sys declares dirty:true; this is retained, and its published archive is not represented as a clean Git checkout or reconstructed historical output.

Sharp constituent notice materials contain the original Expat 2.8.3, cgif 0.5.3 and lcms 2.19.1 copyright/permission texts at their exact release refs and Git commits/trees/blobs. The current lock and matching installed platform package versions.json associate the explicitly scoped named declarations with the retained versions and original recipe; other metadata fields and JSON formatting are not notice-association requirements.

Three original 6bba067 delivery manifests/receipts document the actually observed origins of the retained small component version members for Linux x64, Windows x64 and macOS arm64. They are archived source evidence, not a requirement to reproduce their whole package membership, bytes, runner or old binaries. Windows AOM 3.14.1 and POSIX AOM 3.15.0 remain distinct from Canvas Cargo libaom 3.11.0; the three-MIT notice slice covers only its three named components.

The three named MIT notices do not establish complete constituent licensing or a corresponding-source arrangement for the separately declared LGPL component families or Cairo MPL2.0. Actual applicable terms and source access/recombination arrangements remain separately scoped; whole Cargo/Skia DEPS or historical producer/toolchain replay is not inferred.

The proxy-libintl 0.5 slice holds its complete five-file own Git source and original source archive at the checksum named by the held Windows MXE recipe. STUB_ONLY is preserved. The glibc Linux version field alone does not identify a linked proxy library; source acquisition does not establish final symbol reachability or aggregate relinking.

Cairo 1.18.4 original COPYING, COPYING-LGPL-2.1 and COPYING-MPL-1.1 retain the exact annotated tag, commit, root tree and file blobs. Its dual source grant is separate from the original publisher MPL 2.0 choice and official Mozilla license text. These terms are not complete Cairo source.

The new proxy source and Cairo terms narrow named material gaps without closing the bundled LGPL source/recombination or Cairo source-access arrangement. Generic GPL/LGPL texts are supplied choice materials; neither all Cargo/DEPS entries nor historical toolchain or old binary reproduction is inferred.
